main_body: Snow-roofed log cabin: a large snow-covered roof slope (rows 7-50) over a vertical plank front wall with an arched double door and two lit windows (rows 52-76)
top_band: The roof slope, in white and pale blue-grey snow tones (L 166-249), runs rows 8-50 at x=55. A bright eave band sits at rows ~47-50, with a step to the dark wood wall at row 52.
evidence: The roof is drawn as a large sloped surface seen from above, with horizontal snow-course bands, a roof vent and a thick lighter eave edge. Below it is a separate vertical wall in a darker wood tone with icicles and shadow under the eave. The door is arched and its frame is inset. The windows have sills and snow caps. This reads like the reference houses, whose roof slopes sit above their wall faces. No receding side face is drawn. The top is a real roof surface, not a thin rim.

style.evidence: Snow has about 5 steps (white, pale, light blue-grey, mid, shadow blue) with per-course scallop shading. The wood wall has several browns with plank grain. The door has iron bands and the windows glow. The measured facts: 9 colours per tile against 11 for the stone reference and 18 for the other, 42 distinct colours against 66 and 185, and 0% flat-fill coverage. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is tinted navy or brown and not a black sticker line. Density is a little under the references but has no large flat areas and the craft is comparable. A careful artist would accept it next to the references.
